stimulus_en: A millisecond counter appears inside a box and starts counting. Tap anywhere as soon as you see it.
interval_distribution: uniform random, re-drawn after every response
feedback_after_each_tap_en: The counter stops and shows your time briefly before the box empties again.
valid_response: reaction time of 100 ms or more after the counter appears
false_start: tap before the counter appears, or reaction time under 100 ms; counted, not used in the median
score_rule: median of all valid reaction times in the session, lapses included, false starts excluded

secondary_metrics.response_speed: mean of 1000/RT over valid responses (responses per second)
secondary_metrics.lapses: count of valid responses of 355 ms or more

if_below_minimum: session saved but not scored (null), so it does not count in the 2-of-3 window
baseline_after_practice: mean and SD of median_rt_ms over the first sessions after practice; for the demo, use persona.baseline.pulse_ms
same_time_of_day_en: Suggested right after the morning check-in.
intro_en: Three minutes, tap when the counter appears. It shows how alert you are today compared with your own usual. It is not a test of your abilities.
after_practice_session_en: Practice {n} of 5 done. Your personal range starts after practice.
after_session_en: Saved. Today's median: {median_ms} ms. Your usual: {baseline_ms} ms. Slower days often follow short sleep or a heavy workload.
after_skip_en: No problem. You can do it later or tomorrow.

sources.cite: Basner, Mollicone & Dinges, 2011 (PVT-B: 3 min, 1-4 s intervals, lapse at 355 ms)
Jones et al., 2022 (PVT-B used on the ISS)

note_en: PVT-B-style task. Our implementation copies the format; it is not a validated PVT-B.
